newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal dismayed at snub by ally Britain - paper.
newsitem.headline: Portugal dismayed at snub by ally Britain - paper.

text.p: Portugal is furious with Britain, its oldest political ally, for voting against Lisbon in last week's UN Security Council elections, the respected daily Publico reported on Saturday.
"Our ancient ally did everything within the scope of its powerful diplomatic machine to make Portugal lose the election," Publico wrote.
But the newspaper said Portugal would get its revenge when it made its first speech to the Security Council in French instead of English.

Portugal was elected to the powerful 15-member UN Security Council on Monday for a two-year term beginning in January. Together with Sweden, it beat Australia in a three-cornered race for two seats in the West European and Others group.
"British diplomats wanted Australia, a Commonwealth country, to win," Publico said.
The paper said Spain, France, Italy and Greece had voted for Portugal along with the United States, Russia and China.
Foreign Ministry officials were unavailable to comment on the report but the weekly Expresso echoed the small country's sense of betrayal in its headline: "Big Powers Vote Against Portugal".
Portugal's ties with Britain go back to the 1386 Treaty of Windsor which was signed before the marriage of England's Philippa of Lancaster to Portuguese King Joao I.

The alliance has hit rocky patches in the past but the Anglo-Portuguese relationship usually remained cordial. Publico suggested this might now change: "The time when "always vote with England' was the number one rule of Portuguese diplomacy is over."
